subject: Boundary validation: control/data plane demarcation & egress proofing for VividBank
messages:
From: Luis Garcia <luis.garcia@acmecloud.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: VividBank private deploy - initial boundary diagrams and egress evidence request

Hi Ben / Monica,

Thanks for the quick turn on the draft reference diagram attached (vpc_reference_diagram_v1.pdf). We are doing a pre-audit boundary validation ahead of next week's SOC2 evidence collection and need a short review from Redwood on the control plane vs data plane split and the egress path semantics.

High level asks: 
- Confirm control plane endpoints that will be reachable across the peering (IPs/FQDNs listed on the diagram).
- Confirm whether the data plane nodes will perform SNAT to customer egress or whether we should expect source IP preservation.
- Confirm TLS termination and where mutual TLS is required (control plane only or also data plane egress).
- Provide the operations checklist we can include in the audit (attached ops-checklist-v1.xlsx).

A couple of constraints on our side: VividBank requires explicit egress filtering at the firewall (no 0.0.0.0/0 allowed from data-plane subnets) and per-flow logging that we can ingest into our Splunk instance. We also need to understand if Redwood will supply per-request identifiers for correlation.

Would appreciate a short response by EOD May 20 if possible — if not, we can schedule a 30m call tomorrow to run through the items.

Thanks,

Luis Garcia
Partner Solutions Engineer, AcmeCloud
Attachments: vpc_reference_diagram_v1.pdf, ops-checklist-v1.xlsx
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Luis Garcia <luis.garcia@acmecloud.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 19:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VividBank private deploy - initial boundary diagrams and egress evidence request

Luis — thanks for the diagram and checklist. Quick answers + action items so we can close the pre-audit: 

1) Control plane endpoints:
- Control plane management will terminate on the managed control plane LB in the customer VPC. FQDNs on the diagram (control.redwood.private.vividbank) resolve to the pair of LBs; we will provide the long-lived IP ranges at cutover (we do not change these frequently).

2) Data plane SNAT behavior:
- By default our inference workers will SNAT to a transit gateway IP (per-tenant / per-VPC SNAT IP). We can provide an option to preserve client source IPs via a passthrough configuration but that has implications for autoscaling and connection tracking. For VividBank audit purposes we recommend the explicit SNAT path (so you can whitelist a small set of egress IPs).

3) TLS / mTLS:
- Control plane requires mutual TLS (client cert from VividBank + Redwood server cert).
- Data plane egress (model calls back to customer endpoints) supports TLS but normally not mTLS; if you require mTLS for specific flows we can gate that behind the private deployment options (we'll need the cert exchange and cert rotation plan).

4) Logging / correlation IDs:
- Redwood will emit per-request IDs and include them in logs and response headers for hosted/private deployments. We will provide a log stream (S3 + Kinesis or direct Splunk forwarder) as part of the Ops package.

Action items I will take:
- Attach a short blurb clarifying the SNAT and control-plane LB behavior (see attached ops-checklist-v1-rev1.xlsx).
- Share the minimal IP list for control-plane LBs by EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule a 30-minute design review with your infra lead to confirm firewall rules.

Monica / Marissa — tagging you for any technical caveats or corrections I missed. If VividBank wants to avoid SNAT we should confirm whether they accept ephemeral worker IPs or prefer a NAT hop.

Cheers,

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Luis Garcia <luis.garcia@acmecloud.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 08:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: VividBank private deploy - initial boundary diagrams and egress evidence request

Luis — a few technical clarifications and the specific knobs we normally recommend for regulated customers. Quoting Ben inline where helpful.

- Control plane endpoints (confirming): control.redwood.private.vividbank (LB pair) — we will provide a /27 set for ACLs. Control plane uses mTLS; ports 443 and 8443 for management traffic.

- Data plane behavior (more detail):
  * Worker subnets: 10.200.32.0/22 (data-plane compute)
  * Egress NAT: default is SNAT to tenant-transit IPs assigned per VPC (example: 18.180.100.200). This gives you a consistent egress allowlist with a small set of public IPs.
  * If you need source IP preservation: we can enable passthrough mode but that requires a static pool and explicit connection tracking configuration; autoscaling increases the operational surface. For SOC2 it's cleaner to use SNAT.

- Routing: We recommend advertising a default route to our transit gateway and doing firewall egress rules on the VividBank edge to the SNAT IPs. BGP is optional — many customers use static routes plus health-checked LBs.

- Ports/protocols: Allow outbound 443 and 5222 (if using service-to-service XMPP telemetry) from the worker subnet. Control plane only needs inbound 443 from the VividBank management subnets.

- Observability and evidence:
  * We will push per-request log records to your Splunk collector (TLS) and provide a delivery manifest for audit.
  * We will surface the request-id header (X-Redwood-ReqId) that shows up in the worker logs and in the control plane traces.

I have updated the ops checklist to include the control-plane IP blocks, SNAT policy language, and the log delivery format — see ops-checklist-v1-rev1.xlsx attached. Also created JIRA NETOPS-4123 to track the permit rule changes and evidence collection.

If that all matches what VividBank needs we can have a short handoff call tomorrow morning Pacific and I will upload the final runbook to the Doc link.

Monica Patel
Customer Reliability Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachments: ops-checklist-v1-rev1.xlsx
